hardware.note: One GPU per run, 4 pinned cores per run. Up to four runs concurrently during a time-boxed 4-GPU grant (expired 2026-08-01 02:38); two thereafter. 4x4 = 16 cores, the standing cap.

hyperparameter_origin: paper-reproduction-selected (Sine+Stocks HP search in methods/TimeDiT/paper_reimplementation; no tuning on Heston, train.npy or disc.npy)

model.name: TimeDiT
model.reimplementation_basis: arXiv:2409.02322 App. C -- no official release; DiT-S backbone reimplemented from facebookresearch/DiT

numerical_repair.declared_under: PDF §1.3 (post-hoc transformation, declared) and §1.4 (model-specific numerical repair)
numerical_repair.operator_order: divide-first (apply_s0_repair.py --anchor-exact). The declared multiply-first form leaves a 1.4e-14 residual on this method's banks, which fails PDF §1.4's "begin at S0 = 100" -- stated with no tolerance. Divide-first is exact by construction because x / x is exactly 1.0. The two forms differ by at most 1.8e-15 in log returns, so the choice does not touch the path law; it only decides whether the anchor is exact.
numerical_repair.reason: PDF §1.4 and §7 checklist item 5 require every bank to begin at S0 = 100; the raw generator emits prices in standardized price space and is not anchored at t = 0.

preprocessing.description: Two-stage affine map of raw prices, both stages fitted on train.npy: first x -> (x - min) / (max - min) onto [0,1], then z -> (z - mu) / sigma. Inverted in the same order before saving the bank, with the [0,1] stage clipped to its own range. No log-return transform, no quantile map, no dimensionality reduction.
